content.comment_body: For a single [product_name] project in diagram mode, use lsc. For single or multiple [product_name] projects with partner devices in network mode, use mnp. lnp is for [article_no] standard modules, while mnp is for [version_no] modules.
Thank you [user_name] and [user_name] for your help. One more question: What is the difference between .lsc and .mnp file types in LSC?

Are mnp files managed as a single file? My network program always remains at 98 kB regardless of edits or added blocks, while the same program in lsc format is much larger. I am trying to save it to a USB drive but suspect there are additional files or data I can't see.

As mentioned earlier, the mnp extension is only present when at least one [version_no] module is included. The meaning of this extension is unclear but may stand for Modbus, network, and project. If your file size doesn't change, I can't determine why. You may need to consult someone familiar with the file structure and underlying programming language.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about the roles and distinctions of .lsc and .mnp file types in [product_name] software, notably how they apply to different devices and modes. There is confusion over file sizes and how project files are managed or stored, with no clear documentation or guidance available, making project handling and backup challenging.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want straightforward documentation and explanations for the .lsc and .mnp file types in [product_name] software, clarifying their intended use and compatibility with various devices or modes. They also expect transparent project file management and assurance of data integrity when saving or transferring projects.
